sourcing_note: Prompts are written from the author's reading of how a business owner or consultant would ask for each step (anonymised, no client names or figures). Not captured from live runs. Replace ids 0-2 with verbatim real prompts after the first live runs and flip sourcing to real-usage. Until then the build verdict stays SHIP WITH FLAGS.

evals.prompt: We're a 12-person agency and software costs keep creeping up. I've got a list of what we pay for in a spreadsheet. Which tools could we replace with something we build ourselves?
evals.expected_output: Builds or reads swap/spend.csv, asks for feature counts from the people who use each tool rather than estimating them, runs spend.py, prints the table, names exactly one tool to swap first with its cancel-by date, and lists unknowns under Gaps.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/spend.py and prints its table instead of ranking tools by judgement
Asks for features used out of features offered from the people using each tool
Names exactly one tool under a First swap heading
Has a Gaps section that lists every unknown number

evals.prompt: Here's our card statement for the year. Pull out the software and tell me what we're wasting money on.
evals.expected_output: Extracts tool names and annual costs from the statement, states the currency, marks tools without usage data as NO-DATA, and asks one batched question for seats, active users, feature counts and renewal dates before any ranking.

assertions.text: Asks for the missing columns in one batched message
States the currency instead of inferring it
Marks tools with no usage data as NO-DATA and keeps them off the shortlist
Does not name a tool to replace before usage data exists

evals.prompt: Our biggest line is the payroll provider at 14k a year and we only use a tenth of it. Surely that's the first one to replace?
evals.expected_output: Declines to offer payroll as a swap candidate: the script marks it REGULATED, the answer explains owning it adds legal liability, and it moves to the next candidate or says nothing else is worth swapping.

assertions.text: Says payroll is in a regulated category and is not offered as a swap
Lists the payroll tool under Not offered with its reason
Does not recommend building a payroll system even though utilisation is low

evals.prompt: We renewed our CRM last month, notice period is 90 days, renewal is 2027-03-15. Is it worth looking at replacing it? We pay 9k and use 4 of 40 features.
evals.expected_output: Runs the script with the dates, reports the cancel-by date 2026-12-15 derived from the renewal date and notice days, labels it CANDIDATE, and asks the three questions about users, impact and data export before recommending.

assertions.text: Runs the script rather than computing the date by hand in prose
Asks who uses it, what breaks without it, and whether the data can be exported

evals.prompt: Audit our subscriptions, then just start rebuilding the top five tools straight away.
evals.expected_output: Completes the audit but does not start five rebuilds: it picks one tool to swap first and says each further swap is a separate run through the chain, stopping at the audit output.

assertions.text: Names one tool, not five, as the first swap
Does not begin any build work from the audit step
Explains that parallel swaps stall and the next tool gets its own run
